items.ja: トマトたっぷりバターチキンカレー
items.note: A tomato curry finished with butter and cream, with yoghurt-marinated chicken, served over Tenri-grown rice mixed with black rice, plus a tofu-and-salted-kelp salad. Ask whether the curry is thickened with flour.

items.ja: とろけるチーズチキンカレー
items.note: The same curry base under a blanket of melted cheese; comes with salad. The two curries are the whole curry menu.

items.ja: 天然酵母のハーフサイズピザ
items.romaji: tennen kobo no haafu saizu piza
items.note: Small naturally-leavened pizza — wheat dough. Often shaped and decorated as a cat's face (ねこピザ neko-piza), which is what most of the photos on this shop are of.

items.ja: サンドイッチとドリンクのセット
items.note: Wheat-bread sandwich with a drink.

items.en: Cake of the day with a drink
items.note: Whatever is baked that day plus a drink; around ¥880 if you upgrade the drink. Cakes seen include New York cheesecake, white-chocolate cheesecake, caramel-banana cheesecake and chiffon cake.

items.ja: ニューヨークチーズケーキ
items.note: Dense baked cheesecake on a biscuit base; served with cream and ice cream on a deer-patterned plate.
Price quoted is with a coffee. Airy wheat-flour sponge.
Soft-set egg-and-milk custard with caramel — normally wheat-free by recipe, but this kitchen bakes cakes, so ask.
Rotating parfaits — grape, caramel-orange, banana, black-bean-and-kinako, and a striped 'tora-neko' (tabby cat) one. Usually layered with cornflakes or sponge, so treat as wheat.

items.ja: きんかんとほうじ茶のマフィン
items.note: Sold from the shopfront counter alongside other take-away sweets; hojicha is roasted green tea.
The shop's name means 'four leaves'; a small clover-shaped cookie comes free with drinks.
Price from a 2015 report. Comes with the clover cookie (which is wheat).

items.ja: 自家製レモネードソーダ
items.note: Made in-house.
Served as two visible layers you stir together yourself.
Kansai-style blended banana-and-fruit shake; contains milk.

items.en: Omurice — ketchup-seasoned chicken rice under a soft omelette
items.note: The shop names this and its home-made cakes as its two specialities. The 'torotoro tamago' style means the egg is left barely set and cut open at the table.

items.ja: オムピラフオンカレー
items.note: House speciality — pilaf, omelette and curry sauce in one plate; sold in 'dai' (large) size too. Japanese curry sauce is a wheat-flour roux.

items.ja: ピラフ きのこクリームソース
items.note: A scallop-and-mushroom cream version was reported at ¥850. Cream sauces here are flour-thickened.

items.en: Hayashi rice — beef and onion in a dark demi-glace stew over rice
items.note: Appears on the lunch rotation. Demi-glace is a wheat roux.
Advertised on a board outside; ¥700–¥730 depending on the day. Locals fill the place for it. Fried dishes such as the prawn-cutlet-and-white-fish set turn up on the rotation.

items.ja: エビカツと白身魚のフライ定食
items.romaji: ebikatsu to shiromizakana no furai teishoku
items.en: Prawn cutlet and white-fish fry set meal
items.note: Breadcrumbed and deep-fried; panko is wheat.
Reviewers call it generously filled; also served as one of the three morning-set choices with salad.
Until 11am, every day including Sunday. From about ¥520 — you pay for the drink and add ¥120 for the toast/sandwich/roll set; with a ¥380 blend coffee that lands at ¥500.
One of the morning-set options.
Wheat-batter crêpes with a drink.

items.ja: 自家製カスタードプリン
items.note: The most-photographed thing in the shop — a tall, firm old-school baked custard. Reported at ¥570 in an older review and ¥700 recently; ¥550 more for a drink set.
American coffee about ¥500 in a morning set.
Reported anywhere from ¥200 as part of a meal to ¥350 on its own.
Kansai kissaten staple — banana and tinned fruit blended with milk.

Kezurihi is the word for shaved ice used in Sei Shonagon's Pillow Book — the shop uses the old reading deliberately and names every flavour after a figure from Nara-period history. This is the shop's whole summer identity; flavours below are the individual bowls.
'Ichibiko' is the archaic Japanese word for strawberry.
Named for the princess who became Empress Jito; a blue syrup meant to evoke the water of Yoshino.

Named for Prince Oama (later Emperor Tenmu). Kuzu-mochi is arrowroot-starch jelly; kinako is roasted soybean flour. Ask whether the kuzu is 100% hon-kuzu — cheaper versions are cut with potato starch.
Otomo no Tabito wrote the Manyoshu's famous plum-blossom poems. Contains alcohol.

items.en: Blood orange and liqueur shaved ice ('grown-up' version)
items.note: Eukashi is a chieftain from the Emperor Jimmu legend. Contains alcohol.
Named for the Soga clansman assassinated in 645; sumomo is Japanese plum.
Prince Nagaya's Nara mansion site is a short walk away. Honey and dairy.
Named for the Nara court lady whose surname Tachibana means citrus.
Saohime is the goddess of spring in Nara's Saho hills.

items.en: Clove and loquat-leaf tea shaved ice
items.note: Chujo-hime is the Nara noblewoman of the Taima-dera mandala legend; loquat-leaf tea was a medieval medicinal drink.
Named after ancient tube-and-comma beads; topped with jelly pieces shaped like them. Ask whether the jelly is agar or gelatin.
Taishokkan was the highest court rank, granted to Fujiwara no Kamatari. Contains cheesecake, so wheat and dairy.
Kashikiya-hime is Empress Suiko. Yamato-toki is a Nara-grown medicinal root with a strong herbal flavour.

items.en: Kohaku-to crystal candy and vanilla ice cream shaved ice
items.note: Named for the princess who became Empress Gensho — her name literally contains the character for 'ice'. Kohaku-to is agar jelly dried to a crisp sugar shell.

items.ja: 古代のスイーツ（さくべい・まがり）とドリンクのセット
items.romaji: kodai no suiitsu (sakubei / magari) to dorinku no setto
items.en: Ancient-sweets set (sakubei and magari) with a drink
items.note: Reconstructions of karagashi — Tang-dynasty sweets recorded in Nara-period documents. Sakubei is a twisted rope of dough and magari a ring; both are wheat dough, fried. Genuinely the oldest identifiable confectionery in Japan.
Arrowroot-starch jelly from a Yoshino maker — Yoshino is the historic source of Japan's best kudzu. Clear, wobbly, eaten with kinako and syrup. Ask whether it is 100% hon-kuzu.

items.ja: 卵・牛乳不使用のホットケーキ
items.note: Made without egg or dairy — a rare find in a Japanese cafe — but still wheat flour. Paused during the busy shaved-ice season.

items.ja: メリメロベーキングさんのカヌレ
items.note: Bought in from a local baker. Paused during the shaved-ice season.
Milk boiled down for hours until it sets into a fudge-like block. Recorded as a tribute food in 8th-century Nara and revived from those records; tastes like unsweetened condensed milk.

items.ja: 須恵器でおつまみ（鴨・栗・蘇）
items.en: Snack plate served in Sue-ware (duck, chestnut, so)
items.note: Sueki is the grey unglazed stoneware of the Kofun and Nara periods; the shop serves the snacks in it.

items.ja: コーヒー・カフェオレ
items.note: Café au lait contains dairy.
Black tea made from Japanese tea leaves — milder and sweeter than Indian black tea.
Yuzu citrus preserved in sugar, dissolved in hot water; some brands use honey.
Ume syrup; the non-alcoholic version.
Beer is barley. Sake is rice-brewed but the koji handling is not declared.

items.ja: ホットコーヒー（中深煎り）
items.note: The whole point of the place: a record-playing coffee house where ¥500 gets you a seat with no cover charge. Roast level is chosen at the counter.
One of the named single origins.
Contains dairy.
The house sweet, ordered by almost everyone alongside the coffee. 'Rare' cheesecake in Japan means unbaked and set with gelatin, on a crushed-biscuit base.
The baked version; rich and dense.
Ordered with the dark-roast coffee.

items.ja: ひとくちモナカ（2種セット）
items.en: Bite-size monaka wafer sweets, set of two
items.note: Monaka are crisp wafer shells filled with bean paste — the wafer is made from mochi rice, but the fillings here were raspberry-and-white-bean and walnut-and-sesame-bean. Ask about the shell.

items.ja: おばんざいセット（コース）
items.en: Obanzai set — five to seven small home-style dishes, served one at a time
items.note: This is how the shop works: you order the set and small bowls arrive in sequence, changing daily. Obanzai is Kansai everyday home cooking, not restaurant food. Dashi and soy sauce run through nearly all of it, so assume wheat and fish.

The proprietor holds a SAKE DIPLOMA qualification. There is no written sake list — every bottle on the shelves is orderable; say whether you want it chilled or warmed and what flavour you like, and she offers you candidates. She is a warm-sake specialist.

items.ja: 具材いっぱいの白和え
items.en: Shira-ae — vegetables dressed in mashed tofu and sesame
items.note: Tofu is pounded smooth with white sesame and sugar and used as a dressing. Usually seasoned with a little soy or dashi.

items.ja: 柿と鯛と赤カブのマリネ
items.romaji: kaki to tai to akakabu no marine
items.en: Persimmon, sea bream and red-turnip marinade
items.note: Persimmon is Nara's signature fruit and appears constantly on autumn menus here.

items.en: Chicken gizzard in sweet vinegar marinade
items.note: Nanbanzuke means fried then steeped in vinegar, soy and chilli — the frying dredge and the soy are both wheat.
Grated lotus root formed into dumplings in a dashi broth.
A Chinese-Japanese crossover typical of the kitchen — doubanjiang and soy sauce both carry wheat.

items.ja: あんぽ柿クリームチーズの天婦羅
items.en: Semi-dried persimmon and cream cheese tempura
items.note: Anpo-gaki is persimmon dried only part-way, so it stays soft and jammy. Tempura batter is wheat.

items.ja: 鰻と梨のカマンベール春巻き
items.romaji: unagi to nashi no kamanbeeru harumaki
items.en: Eel, pear and camembert spring roll
items.note: Spring-roll wrappers are wheat.

items.ja: わさび菜入りサーモンのなめろう
items.note: Namero is raw fish chopped on the board with miso and aromatics until it is almost a paste — a fisherman's dish. Miso can be barley-based.

items.ja: 牛スジとこんにゃくの筑前煮
items.en: Beef tendon and konnyaku simmered Chikuzen-style
items.note: Chikuzen-ni is root vegetables browned then simmered in soy and mirin.

items.ja: 玄米リゾット粕汁添え
items.note: Kasujiru is soup enriched with sake lees — the residue left after pressing sake. Mildly alcoholic and warming; a winter staple in this region.
Surinagashi is a vegetable puréed and thinned with dashi — served as the opening warm or cold bowl.
Grilled rice cake topped with salted, dried mullet roe — a Kyoto-style luxury snack for sake.

items.ja: ブルーチーズハムカツ
items.note: Served by the quarter. Panko-crumbed and fried.

items.ja: 大人のお子さまランチ
items.note: The signature. A children's-plate layout done properly for adults: chicken rice under an omelette, hamburg steak, a prawn fry, Napolitan spaghetti, salad and soup, with the custard pudding added for the full price. Lunchtime only. There is a cat-shaped version too.

items.ja: ひよこ豆のカレー（for vegan）
items.note: The shop labels this one 'for vegan' on its own menu — unusual in a Nara kissaten. Confirm the spice paste and any soy seasoning if you need it gluten-free.
Spice-based minced-chicken curry rather than Japanese roux, but confirm.
Poached chicken breast on rice with a spring-onion-and-ginger sauce, plus black soy and sweet chilli on the side, with soup. Paused in winter. Soy sauce is wheat.

Nara's own zoni: white miso broth with round mochi and root vegetables — and the local twist is that you pull the mochi out and dip it in kinako (sweet roasted soybean flour) before eating. Miso may be barley-based.

items.ja: きのこあんかけハンバーグ
items.note: A daily lunch special. Hamburg patties in Japan are bound with panko, and ankake sauce is soy-based and starch-thickened.
Served all year, not just summer. Around ¥1,000–¥1,500 depending on the flavour.

items.ja: アボカドミルクと木の実
items.note: Seasonal. Contains dairy.

items.ja: ラズベリーミルク・ピスタチオ
items.en: Raspberry milk and pistachio shaved ice

items.ja: 喫茶店の苺ミックスジュースかき氷
items.romaji: kissaten no ichigo mikkusu juusu kakigori
items.note: Built to taste like the old kissaten mixed fruit juice.
Also served as 抹茶ミルクあずき with sweet red beans.

items.ja: 黒蜜きなこぷりんかき氷
items.en: Brown-sugar syrup, kinako and pudding shaved ice
items.note: Kuromitsu is unrefined-sugar syrup; kinako is roasted soybean flour.

items.ja: パンプキンチャイかき氷
items.note: Autumn flavour.
The shop's pudding, decorated as a black cat. Plain custard is wheat-free by recipe but the kitchen fries and bakes.
There is also an omurice morning set.
From 5pm the front room becomes a sake bar under a different name. Seen: aosa-seaweed potato salad, simmered kombu strips with fried tofu, and Okinawan shima-rakkyo with miso.
Narazuke is Nara's signature pickle — melon or gourd cured for months in sake lees. It is genuinely alcoholic and strongly so; not for drivers or children. Paired here with rich monkfish liver.

items.ja: 日本酒（奈良の地酒中心・14種）
items.en: Sake — about 14 kinds, mostly Nara breweries
items.note: Nara is where sake brewing as we know it was formalised, in the temple breweries of Shoryaku-ji. Shochu, gin and whisky are also poured.
Simmered in dashi and soy; fish-cake items contain wheat.

items.ja: 白子とほうれん草のキッシュ
items.note: Shirako is cod milt — creamy and mild. Pastry is wheat.

items.ja: カトゥレット（スリランカのコロッケ）
items.note: Deep-fried spiced fish-and-potato balls; breadcrumbed.

The shop's flagship, and its allergen line lists none of the eight major allergens. Fine wasanbon sugar pressed into thin tablets that dissolve on the tongue. Named by Prince Arisugawa after 'aoni-yoshi', the fixed poetic epithet for the city of Nara itself. Price is for a 5-piece box; ¥4,600 for 10, ¥8,300 for 18.
Ten smaller tablets. Allergen line: none declared.
The same sugar cake with sesame worked in. The shop declares sesame as the only allergen.

Modelled on the paper camellias the monks make for Todaiji's Omizutori rite each March, and invented by this shop — many imitations exist. Shop's allergen line: egg only. Two-day shelf life; sold only in season, 3 pieces for ¥2,890.
Named for the holy water drawn from the Wakasa well during Todaiji's Omizutori. Sold in assortments with the Roben camellia. Two-day shelf life; no allergens declared.

items.en: Kuzu-zakura — bean paste in arrowroot jelly
items.note: Red bean paste wrapped in translucent kudzu (arrowroot) starch jelly and a salted cherry leaf. Yoshino in southern Nara is Japan's classic source of kudzu. Shop declares no allergens. Six pieces ¥1,350.
Named for Asuka, the capital before Nara. A gentle salt note to cut the sweetness; 30-day shelf life. Shop declares no allergens. Nine pieces ¥1,500.
Crisp rice-flour wafers shaped as deer, filled with the shop's own bean paste — the deer of Nara Park were revered as messengers of the gods. Shop declares no allergens. Five pieces ¥2,100.
Purple, white, red, yellow and green — the five colours of the banners hung across great temple halls. Six sheets ¥2,160. No allergens declared.
An assortment of moulded dry sugar sweets whose shapes change with the season; made for the tea ceremony. Ten pieces ¥2,200. No allergens declared.

items.en: Kenjo Mikasa — large dorayaki-style bean-paste pancake
items.note: 'Mikasa' is the Kansai word for dorayaki, named after Nara's Mount Mikasa which the round cakes resemble. Shop's allergen line: wheat flour and egg. One piece ¥1,550.

items.en: Small Mikasa with the crane brand mark
items.note: A more manageable size, branded with the shop's standing-crane crest. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Five pieces ¥2,200.

items.en: Yumedono — octagonal sweet after Horyu-ji's Hall of Dreams
items.note: Shaped after the octagonal Yumedono at Horyu-ji, associated with Prince Shotoku. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Six pieces ¥3,000.
Despite 'senbei' usually meaning rice crackers, the shop's own allergen line reads wheat flour and egg — these are the wheat-flour kind. Eight packs ¥1,620.
Rustic old-Yamato flavour. Allergens declared by the shop: wheat flour, egg and peanut. Eight pieces in a bag ¥1,188.
The Portuguese-derived honey sponge cake. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Sold by length — three sun (about 9cm) ¥3,600 up to six sun ¥7,200.
The castella batter rolled. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Small ¥2,070, large ¥4,140.
A boxed pairing of Kyokusui-no-en and Asuka-kokyo. Allergens: wheat flour, egg.
Summer jelly sweets, 60-day shelf life. Six pieces ¥2,538. No allergen line published for this one — ask.

items.ja: 風味・3色・貝中しるこ
items.en: Instant shiruko — sweet red-bean soup in a wafer shell
items.note: A wafer shell you drop in a bowl and pour hot water over; it collapses into sweet red-bean soup. The 'kaichu' version comes in a clam-shaped shell. No allergen line published — ask about the wafer.

items.en: 'Yoshino River sweetfish' — bean-paste sweet in fish form
items.note: A summer sweet shaped as an ayu, the river fish caught in the Yoshino. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Availability has been intermittent — ask.
Roasted by the method the founding owner used, still followed. Prices start around ¥400.
The thing people come for, and a remarkable ¥150 — but it cannot be ordered on its own; you must order a drink with it.
Described in a guidebook as idiosyncratic. Japanese curry roux is wheat-based.

items.ja: ビール＆おつまみセット
items.note: The place looks like an izakaya from outside and a machiya inside; beer with one snack is a set at ¥900. Beer is barley.
